entries.title: Washington State Court Grants Preliminary Injunction Against Kalshi for Violations of State Gambling Act and Consumer Protection Act
entries.facts: King County Superior Court (Washington state) granted a preliminary injunction against Kalshi on July 20, 2026, finding that Kalshi's prediction market contracts likely violate both the Washington Gambling Act and the Consumer Protection Act. The court found that Kalshi's event contracts — covering sports, elections, natural disasters, and other contingent events — constitute gambling under Washington law, which defines gambling as staking or risking something of value upon the outcome of a contest of chance or a future contingent event, and prohibits internet gambling as amended in 2006. The court also ruled that Kalshi's marketing constitutes unfair and deceptive acts or practices under the Consumer Protection Act, citing a Kalshi advertisement in which a user texts about finding 'a way to bet on the NFL even though we live in Washington.' Washington AG Nick Brown filed the underlying complaint on March 27, 2026. The court will issue a final injunction order setting full remedies on August 5, 2026. Washington is reported as the 4th state to obtain a preliminary injunction against Kalshi's sports event contracts, with state regulators and courts prevailing in 19 of 23 such decisions nationally.
